# Default settings for the upload service. device-logs.aws.region and device-logs.storage.bucket
# have no default here. Each environment sets them in cloud8-config-service-backend, and the app
# does not start without them.
#
# Still to add:
# - server.tomcat.keep-alive-timeout: 130 s (longer than the ALB idle timeout of 120 s).
# - server.shutdown: graceful.
# - device-logs.* defaults: rate limit 30 per 10 min, in-flight cap 200.
server:
  port: 1296
  # Stops Tomcat's RemoteIpValve, which Spring Boot adds on Kubernetes, from moving the ALB's
  # X-Forwarded-For entry into getRemoteAddr() before AlbHeaderTrust reads it (ADR 0004).
  # Don't override this or cloud8.config.forwarded-headers in cloud8-config-service-backend.
  forward-headers-strategy: none
spring:
  mvc:
    formcontent:
      filter:
        # Stops FormContentFilter reading a PUT body sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded before
        # the checks run, which would also make Tomcat send 100 Continue (ADR 0009).
        enabled: false
  servlet:
    multipart:
      # Stops DispatcherServlet parsing a multipart/* body before it picks the handler, for the same
      # reason. Phones never send multipart.
      enabled: false
management:
  server:
    port: 1297
device-logs:
  # The names AWS gives the headers the ALB adds after the mTLS handshake.
  trust:
    subject: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Subject
    issuer: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Issuer
    validity: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Validity
    serial-number: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Serial-Number
    leaf: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Leaf
    forwarded-for: X-Forwarded-For
  # One entry per contract FileType, or the app does not start. A disabled type gets 403, and a
  # Content-Length above max-size gets 413.
  file-types:
    app-log:
      enabled: true
      max-size: 10MB
    boot-log:
      enabled: true
      max-size: 10MB
    # Personal data. Stays off until the privacy review says yes (ADR 0008).
    calls-xml:
      enabled: false
      max-size: 10MB
  storage:
    # Below the ALB idle timeout of 120 s, so the phone hears 429 from the service instead of a
    # timeout from the ALB. Change it together with the ALB and Tomcat values (ADR 0005).
    write-timeout: 60s
cloud8:
  config:
    # Stops cloud8's ForwardedHeaderFilter from removing X-Forwarded-For before AlbHeaderTrust
    # reads it (ADR 0004).
    forwarded-headers:
      enabled: false
  security:
    # Replaces cloud8's /public/** default, so it is listed again. cloud8 turns CSRF off for
    # every public path, and phones carry no JWT.
    public-paths:
      - /public/**
      - /logs/**

file.content:
# Envoy as the ALB stand-in for a real phone. It checks the phone's chain against the Poly CAs and
# rejects anything else in the TLS handshake, adds the headers the ALB adds, streams /logs/ to
# upload-service, and serves the master config the phone fetches at boot. Local runs only.
static_resources:
  listeners:
    - name: phones
      address:
        socket_address: { address: 0.0.0.0, port_value: 8443 }
      filter_chains:
        - transport_socket:
            name: envoy.transport_sockets.tls
            typed_config:
              "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.transport_sockets.tls.v3.DownstreamTlsContext
              # A client without a certificate the Poly CAs signed never gets an HTTP response.
              require_client_certificate: true
              common_tls_context:
                tls_params:
                  tls_minimum_protocol_version: TLSv1_2
                  tls_maximum_protocol_version: TLSv1_3
                  # The ECDHE GCM suites of ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06 (ADR 0003). Every lab
                  # phone offers the two RSA ones, and only on TLS 1.2.
                  cipher_suites:
                    - ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
                    - ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
                    - ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
                    - ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
                # Made by gen-certs.sh for the Mac's LAN IP, the address the phone connects to.
                tls_certificates:
                  - certificate_chain: { filename: /etc/envoy/certs/server.crt }
                    private_key: { filename: /etc/envoy/certs/server.key }
                validation_context:
                  trusted_ca: { filename: /etc/envoy/poly-ca-bundle.pem }
          filters:
            - name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
              typed_config:
                "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
                stat_prefix: phones
                # Appends the address Envoy saw to X-Forwarded-For, as the ALB does. Through Colima
                # that is a Docker gateway address, not the phone's.
                use_remote_address: true
                xff_num_trusted_hops: 0
                # Envoy answers Expect: 100-continue itself by default, so the phone would send the
                # body before upload-service checks the headers. This passes the Expect on, and
                # upload-service sends 100 Continue only once every check passes (ADR 0009).
                proxy_100_continue: true
                # The ALB idle timeout (ADR 0005).
                stream_idle_timeout: 120s
                common_http_protocol_options:
                  idle_timeout: 120s
                access_log:
                  - name: envoy.access_loggers.stdout
                    typed_config:
                      "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.access_loggers.stream.v3.StdoutAccessLog
                      log_format:
                        text_format_source:
                          inline_string: "[%START_TIME%] %REQ(:METHOD)% %REQ(:PATH)% %RESPONSE_CODE% %RESPONSE_FLAGS% in=%BYTES_RECEIVED% out=%BYTES_SENT% %DURATION%ms peer=\"%DOWNSTREAM_PEER_SUBJECT%\"\n"
                http_filters:
                  - name: envoy.filters.http.router
                    typed_config:
                      "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.router.v3.Router
                route_config:
                  virtual_hosts:
                    - name: phones
                      domains: ["*"]
                      routes:
                        - match: { prefix: /logs/ }
                          route:
                            cluster: upload_service
                            # No deadline, like the ALB. Envoy's default of 15 s, counted from the
                            # end of the body, would cut off the S3 write, which may take 60 s
                            # (ADR 0005). The idle timeout above still applies.
                            timeout: 0s
                          # Removed before the headers below are added, so a copy a client sent
                          # never reaches upload-service.
                          request_headers_to_remove:
                            - X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert
                            - X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Subject
                            - X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Issuer
                            - X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Validity
                            - X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Serial-Number
                            - X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Leaf
                          # The ALB's mTLS headers, from the phone's leaf certificate.
                          request_headers_to_add:
                            - header: { key: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Subject, value: "%DOWNSTREAM_PEER_SUBJECT%" }
                            - header: { key: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Issuer, value: "%DOWNSTREAM_PEER_ISSUER%" }
                            - header:
                                key: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Validity
                                value: "NotBefore=%DOWNSTREAM_PEER_CERT_V_START(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)%;NotAfter=%DOWNSTREAM_PEER_CERT_V_END(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)%"
                            - header: { key: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Serial-Number, value: "%DOWNSTREAM_PEER_SERIAL%" }
                            # URL-encoded PEM, as the ALB sends it.
                            - header: { key: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Leaf, value: "%DOWNSTREAM_PEER_CERT%" }
                        # <mac>.cfg and 000000000000.cfg. Every phone gets the same master config.
                        - match:
                            safe_regex: { regex: "^/[0-9a-f]{12}\\.cfg$" }
                            headers:
                              - name: ":method"
                                string_match: { exact: GET }
                          direct_response:
                            status: 200
                            body: { filename: /etc/envoy/master.cfg }
                          response_headers_to_add:
                            - header: { key: Content-Type, value: application/xml }
                        # Everything else, like the ALB's default action.
                        - match: { prefix: / }
                          direct_response: { status: 404 }
  clusters:
    - name: upload_service
      type: STRICT_DNS
      connect_timeout: 5s
      # Closes idle connections to upload-service after 120 s, as the ALB does (ADR 0005). Envoy's
      # default is 1 h, longer than Tomcat keeps them open.
      typed_extension_protocol_options:
        envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.upstreams.http.v3.HttpProtocolOptions
          common_http_protocol_options: { idle_timeout: 120s }
          explicit_http_config: { http_protocol_options: {} }
      load_assignment:
        cluster_name: upload_service
        endpoints:
          - lb_endpoints:
              - endpoint:
                  address:
                    socket_address: { address: upload-service, port_value: 1296 }

content.text:
Raising the S3 deadline to 150 s on its own breaks ADR 0005. That ADR fixes the order **S3 write < ALB idle < Tomcat keep-alive** and says to change all three together. So the ALB idle timeout has to go above 150 s and Tomcat keep-alive above that, e.g. 150 / 180 / 190.

Changing these numbers changes an accepted ADR, and the ALB value sits in the Helm ingress settings. The repo's rules say a person must approve that first.

## Where each value is set

| Value | Now | Where |
|---|---|---|
| S3 write deadline | 60 s | `upload-service/src/main/resources/application.yml:55` (`device-logs.storage.write-timeout`). It reaches the SDK as `apiCallTimeout` in `storage/s3/S3ClientConfig.java:30` |
| ALB idle timeout | 120 s | Only described so far, in the comment in `upload-service/src/main/helm/device-log-upload-service-chart/values.yaml:7`. No value is set yet. |
| Tomcat keep-alive | 130 s | **Not set yet.** It's on the "Still to add" list in `application.yml:6` (`server.tomcat.keep-alive-timeout`). |
| Local ALB stand-in | 120 s | `local/envoy/envoy.yaml:47,49` (listener `stream_idle_timeout`, `idle_timeout`) and `:115` (upstream `idle_timeout`) |
